title: Ashen Realm — Complete Visual and Asset Overhaul
instruction_to_codex: When the user asks you to execute this brief, develop the required upgrade end to end in the existing Ashen Realm project. Inspect the actual source first, implement a playable reference encounter, then extend the validated asset and rendering standards to all five chambers and all three character archetypes. Deliver code, actual usable assets, validation evidence, and a reviewable build. Do not stop at another plan or present concept images, fallback geometry, or an untested build as the completed overhaul. Follow the executing environment's higher-priority instructions, available capabilities, project instructions, and applicable skills. Creating this JSON file does not itself execute these tasks or authorize publication.

objective.outcome: A materially more believable, cohesive, cinematic dark-fantasy browser RPG with improved character geometry, physical materials, room lighting, environment detail, animation presentation, effects, and sustained iPhone usability.
objective.visual_thesis: A torchlit burial fortress: cold stone, worn steel, porous bone, oxblood cloth, restrained embers, and darkness that preserves combat readability.
objective.completion_scope: All five existing dungeon chambers, Ash Knight player and Keeper presentation, Crypt Warden enemies, and Ember Sovereign boss presentation.
objective.first_reviewable_result: One finished chamber containing a rebuilt Ash Knight and one rebuilt Crypt Warden, with all four attacks working against actual weapon-contact checks.
success_definition: Improved silhouettes, anatomy, material separation, lighting depth, and motion are visible at the same render resolution as the baseline.
The entire dungeon follows the reference encounter's visual standard.
Visual weapons, attack phases, damage, and reactions remain synchronized.
Measured device performance meets the agreed target profile or any shortfall is explicitly documented.
Guest progression, saves, equipment, dungeon gates, mobile controls, and renderer recovery remain functional.
Missing assets, unavailable device tests, and incomplete features are disclosed rather than presented as finished.

project.name: Ashen Realm

known_good_release.interpretation: Historical verified baseline, not evidence of the current remote HEAD or of validation for the new overhaul. The combat document's original publication caveat predates the later successful deployment.

existing_stack.application: Existing React/TypeScript application and Sites/Vinext hosting structure
existing_stack.persistence: Existing progress API, guest session handling, and D1-backed progression

recovery_instructions: Use the established checkout if present. Inspect its status, applicable AGENTS.md files, manifest, package scripts, and current source before editing.
Verify that the manifest identifies the selected Ashen Realm Site. Reconcile a mismatch; never silently create a replacement Site.
If the checkout is unavailable, use the supported Sites source-recovery workflow and exact returned identifiers.
Treat paths and remote details here as recovery hints. Do not overwrite a newer implementation or force-reset to the historical commit.
Preserve unrelated user changes and use an isolated checkout when appropriate.
Use runtime-provided credentials through supported workflows; never place credentials in this brief, source files, logs, or remote URLs.

execution_policy.source_of_truth: Current project source and supported runtime capabilities, reconciled with this brief.
execution_policy.progress: Maintain a concise task plan and record completed work, evidence, blockers, and remaining acceptance gates.
scope_control: Preserve the existing engine, hosting foundation, five-chamber layout, progression, and combat rules.
Avoid dependency or framework migrations unrelated to an identified upgrade need.
Do not perform paid purchases, hire external artists, or send messages to other people without specific authorization.
Do not change the Site audience or deploy this overhaul solely because a previous combat release was authorized for publication.
Technical stage gates are quality checks, not mandatory design interviews. Continue useful independent work when a gate depends on an unavailable device or asset.
If a genuine asset-production or access blocker remains, complete all feasible integration and validation work, preserve it, and report the exact missing deliverable.
Do not claim Unreal Engine feature parity, motion capture, measured physical materials, or device performance without corresponding evidence.
execution_policy.current_request_scope: Export one self-contained JSON instruction file; do not modify or publish the game while performing this export.
execution_policy.default_future_delivery: Verified implementation, durable source/assets, packaged reviewable build, and a saved Site version using the applicable workflow.
execution_policy.future_publication: Publish only when the executing user's request authorizes deployment to the selected Site and audience. If already authorized, complete publication without asking for duplicate conversational permission.
execution_policy.full_rollout_rule: The reference encounter is an early milestone, not the final scope. Expand to the complete required dungeon after the relevant gates pass; clearly label any unverified rollout if physical-device evidence is unavailable.

observed_baseline.evidence_type: Source and asset inspection; not a new rendered-image audit or GPU benchmark.
observed_baseline.character_construction: Articulated groups containing spheres, cylinders, extruded plates, and merged static pieces per joint/material.

skin_source.method: Mirrored crops from generated concept artwork with luminance-derived relief, not measured PBR scans.

observed_baseline.model_count_caveat: Counts exclude each actor's separate weapon trail and do not measure complete-frame draw cost.

environment.material_loading: Surface texture quality tiers already exist.
environment.geometry: One globally merged structural BVH mesh plus separate ribs, pilasters, niches, and some instanced edging.

mobile_foundation: Touch devices default to Auto unless an explicit saved preference overrides it.
Adaptive output resolution and quality-dependent textures, lights, shadows, AO, and reflections.
Safe-area-aware portrait and compact landscape controls.
Independent movement and combat pointer ownership.
Rendering suspension while paused or hidden.
Graphics-loss recovery and bounded save-request handling.
hypotheses_to_measure: Asset construction and material authorship are stronger realism constraints than another global output-resolution increase.
Material/joint fragmentation and separate repeated scenery are candidates for draw-call reduction.
Generic environment lighting and a moving key light may reduce the visual plausibility of an enclosed crypt.

gameplay: Keep the solo five-chamber dungeon, chamber order, walkable routes, closed-gate rules, shrine checkpoints, equipment, loot, rewards, and boss unlock requirements.
Keep enemy IDs, boss encounter identity, save ownership, guest access, revision conflict handling, and progression schema.
Ember Sovereign remains the visual skin of the existing Hollow King encounter; do not rename saved gameplay IDs.
Do not alter balance values solely to accommodate an asset's exported scale.
Decorative rubble, chipped floors, and set dressing must not introduce accidental navigation obstacles or unsupported floor-height changes.
input_and_lifecycle: Keep simultaneous movement and combat, hold-to-strike, joystick sprint outside melee, labeled touch controls, notch/home-indicator clearance, and compact landscape behavior.
Do not cancel valid gestures when Safari toolbars resize the viewport.
Preserve pointer cancellation, blur/orientation resets, pause/background suspension, renderer disposal, and recovery.
Honor explicit graphics preferences and reduced-motion preferences.
Keep the HUD readable and attacks visible; effects must not obscure control targets.

baseline_combat.status: Already implemented and published; preserve and adapt to new rigs.
damage_authority: Only the active contact window deals melee damage; pressing Attack alone never damages a target.
Sample the rendered weapon pose at intervals no larger than 1/120 second inside each frame's active interval.
Use weapon segment versus target capsule tests, once per target per swing and within the move's target limit.
Clip weapon reach at blocking geometry and retain line-of-sight and behind-player exclusions.
Keep aim assistance in the forward hemisphere and lock facing for the swing.
Keep animation and gameplay on one authoritative phase timeline.

enemy_rules.strike_variants: Cycle all four strike types with visible telegraphs.
enemy_rules.interruption: Wardens can be interrupted before or after active contact; committed active strikes retain momentum.
enemy_rules.boss: Preserve stagger resistance and the three-shrine shield requirement.
enemy_rules.stale_swings: Cancel when enemies leave the animation range so returning enemies do not resume invisible attacks.

presentation.trail_behavior: A short, low-opacity ribbon follows the actual weapon and is hidden in Performance mode or for reduced motion.
presentation.hits: Retain sound, recoil, and readable contact feedback while upgrading their assets.

cancellation_and_overlap: Casting and melee must not overlap.
Normal Strike release stops continuous attacks but preserves one deliberately buffered tap.
Pointer cancellation, lost ownership, pause, and input reset clear held state and queued input.
Death and respawn clear the combat sequence and stale effects.
baseline_combat.reconciliation: Verify these values against current source before integration. If newer user-authored balance changes exist, preserve them and document the discrepancy rather than overwriting them.

priorities: Large forms, anatomy, armor construction, and weapon silhouettes before fine scratches.
Clearly different responses for steel, leather, chainmail, bone, soot, cloth, and damp stone.
Strong foreground, middle-ground, and background depth with clear chamber focal points.
Readable enemy and weapon silhouettes at moderate phone brightness.
Consistent world scale, texel density, wear direction, and material palette.

palette.threat_identifier: Amber eyes and restrained ember emission
palette.lighting: Warm torch sources with controlled cool environmental contrast

requirements.name: Reproducible baseline and quality benchmark
tasks: Record fixed entrance, close-character, Warden-combat, water, and boss camera positions.
Record resolution, quality profile, exposure, content state, frame pacing, and asset version for every comparison.
Add developer-facing counters or reports for main-pass and complete-frame draws/triangles, frame-time distributions, texture inventory, and loading behavior.
Keep diagnostic implementation details out of normal game flows.
Capture visual and device evidence using supported tooling when available; label unavailable measurements.
acceptance: Before/after comparisons use identical camera, resolution, and exposure conditions.
The report distinguishes measured values, estimated allocation sizes, and proposed budgets.
No existing gameplay or production behavior changes merely to create the baseline.

requirements.name: Complete rigged character assets
tasks: Retain the existing Higgsfield character identities and obtain consistent front, side, and back references only where necessary.
Sculpt or adapt properly licensed base meshes; retopologize and author UVs for each asset.
Bake high-detail geometry to the game mesh and author model-specific material maps.
Rig and weight complete 3D volumes, including unseen sides, hands, armor, and weapon attachments.
Export optimized GLBs and explicit lower-detail variants.
Validate any generated 3D export against the same contract; a reference image, flat cutout, or textured primitive does not satisfy the finished asset requirement.
If manual art production is required and unavailable, document the missing deliverable and keep the integration and fallback functional.
acceptance: All three archetypes pass 360-degree and neutral-light inspection.
Shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees deform without unacceptable collapse or armor clipping.
Weapon sockets, scale, bounds, clip inventory, and license/source records are supplied.
The Keeper receives the appropriate Ash Knight-derived presentation while preserving its role.

requirements.name: Rig adapter and animation integration
tasks: Introduce an adapter for pose evaluation, animation state, weapon base/tip sockets, bounds, and resource cleanup.
Retain the current procedural rig as a clearly identified failure fallback.
Map authored side, diagonal, backhand, and overhead clips to the existing phase timeline.
Evaluate weapon collision at the same subframe poses used to define the visible swing.
Use in-place animation initially; retain collision-aware root travel in gameplay code.
Share geometry and material assets while retaining independent skeletons and animation state.
Preserve named nodes and sockets through optimization.
Blend directional locomotion, turn-in-place, pelvis weight shifts, and modest cape motion without changing attack commitment.
acceptance: No double root motion, wall-crossing lunge, duplicated damage clock, or cross-instance animation leakage.
All four moves reach the expected target capsules and obey their current stamina/timing rules.
Visual weapon contact agrees with damage at tested low and high frame rates.
Fallback loads, cancellation, death, respawn, and disposal remain correct.

requirements.name: Physical material authoring and color management
tasks: Replace concept-crop material swatches with authored base color, tangent-space normal, packed occlusion/roughness/metallic, and optional emissive maps.
Do not bake lighting or highlights into base color or infer final geometry from image brightness alone.
Use geometry for visible outlines, chipped profiles, and deep armor separation; normal maps for shallow surface detail.
Use sRGB for color/emissive maps and data color spaces for normals and material controls.
Verify packed-map channel conventions in the exporter and runtime.
Use MeshStandardMaterial by default; enable clearcoat or sheen only where its visual benefit justifies the per-pixel cost.
Size maps by screen coverage and UV usage, preserving suitable existing Poly Haven masonry.
Validate custom shaders, lightmaps, tone mapping, and output conversion as one pipeline.
acceptance: Materials remain convincing under neutral and dungeon lighting.
Steel, cloth, bone, and damp stone remain visually distinguishable.
No incorrect map channel, inverted normal, double color conversion, severe seam, or accidental universal gloss.
Higher resolution is not used to mask inappropriate source materials.

requirements.name: Motivated lighting, lightmaps, and probes
tasks: Replace the generic studio-like environment with a coherent crypt environment.
Tune exposure, fill, torch contribution, shadow softness, and emissive intensity together.
Bake static indirect lighting for fixed architecture using an appropriate offline workflow such as Blender Cycles.
Provide a dedicated non-overlapping lightmap UV set and explicitly bind the correct texture channel after export.
Keep albedo and baked irradiance responsibilities separate to avoid double multiplication.
Exclude moving actors and state-changing gates from static shadow bakes.
Handle shrine activation without ghost colored lighting from the previous state.
Prototype one dominant dynamic shadow source near combat, motivated by an actual light source.
Fade and stabilize dynamic light selection rather than abruptly popping between nearest torches.
Add matched reflection environments and diffuse probe data for moving actors; implement room lookup and transitions explicitly.
Separate baked and dynamic contributions so the same illumination is not counted twice.
Keep modest readability fill where required without relying on an obvious player-following key light.
acceptance: Room depth and material separation improve at unchanged output resolution.
Enemy wind-ups remain readable on a phone.
Gate and shrine state changes leave no visibly invalid baked shadows or lighting.
Room transitions do not cause objectionable light or reflection popping.
Shadow and probe features meet their selected quality-tier budgets.

requirements.name: Modular dungeon architecture and set dressing
tasks: Author a reusable architectural kit covering walls, corners, pillars, arches, vaults, floor slabs, broken edges, and burial alcoves.
Add a bounded shared prop kit emphasizing torches, braziers, sarcophagi, urns, chains, banners, rubble, and throne detail.
Use local stains, vertex tinting, and a small number of stone variants to reduce repetition.
Preserve material scale and wear direction across module seams.
Give all five existing chambers distinct focal arrangements through composition and lighting.
Keep existing walkable routes, combat lanes, interaction points, gates, and checkpoint positions intact.
Retain provenance and verify redistribution rights for every external asset.
acceptance: Each chamber is visually identifiable without requiring many unique material sets.
Set dressing improves depth and history without hiding enemies or creating accidental collision.
No visible scale discontinuity, floating prop, severe repeating seam, or z-fighting at ordinary camera distances.
All existing objectives remain reachable.

requirements.name: Fire, atmosphere, impacts, and trails
tasks: Replace sphere flames with compact authored flame/smoke atlas assets and coordinated flicker.
Pool sparks and debris with bounded capacity, short lifetimes, and shared resources.
Use material-appropriate impact responses such as metal sparks, bone dust, and restrained ember bursts.
Add sparse dust and localized haze only where composition benefits.
Limit temporary impact marks and prevent z-fighting or unbounded accumulation.
Preserve narrow, short weapon trails attached to actual sampled weapon motion.
Profile screen coverage and transparent overdraw as well as particle count.
Respect reduced-motion settings and keep attack telegraphs and touch controls unobscured.
acceptance: Effects respond at the correct contact moment and do not obscure attacks.
Repeated combat does not cause unbounded object or resource growth.
Effect quality scales down cleanly on Performance and Auto profiles.
Fire reads as rising flame rather than a stretched opaque sphere.

requirements.name: Camera framing and restrained postprocessing
tasks: Evaluate asset detail at actual play distance and test closer, better-composed character framing.
Retain wall-aware camera collision and visibility of incoming attacks.
Keep exposure stable and bloom concentrated on luminous surfaces.
Compare antialiasing and sharpening during motion, not only screenshots.
Keep costly AO and planar reflections optional and profile their complete cost.
Do not default to heavy depth of field, motion blur, film grain, chromatic aberration, or constant camera shake.
acceptance: Framing improves appreciation of character assets without compromising navigation or combat awareness.
No camera-wall penetration or new corner-collapse behavior.
Postprocessing preserves material detail, readable blacks, stable edges, and visible telegraphs.

requirements.name: Repeatable asset optimization and delivery
tasks: Use GLTFLoader integration compatible with the installed Three.js version.
Use KTX2/Basis textures with hardware detection and a bounded worker count.
Test UASTC for normals and packed material maps; evaluate ETC1S where quality remains acceptable.
Ship a separately loadable lower-resolution fallback bundle where required compressed extensions prevent an embedded fallback.
Keep compatible decoder JavaScript/WASM files versioned with the game.
Use glTF Transform inspection and selected optimization stages rather than blindly flattening or joining all nodes.
Use Meshopt for transfer compression where suitable; use geometry simplification and batching for runtime cost reduction.
Preserve uncompressed editable masters and compress near the end of the pipeline.
Create an asset manifest containing versions, hashes, source/license data, geometry counts, texture dimensions and color spaces, rig sockets, and clip metadata.
Validate assets and handle warnings explicitly before packaging.
acceptance: Compressed assets load with the expected decoders and preserve essential rig nodes.
Fallback paths are exercised and remain playable.
Optimization produces recorded size/resource changes without unacceptable visual damage.
No unversioned external decoder dependency or secret is included in shipped assets.

requirements.name: Room visibility, batching, streaming, and ownership
tasks: Split visible architecture into room-sized render chunks while retaining a separate safe collision representation.
Instance repeated props within useful room/material batches.
Avoid global batches that defeat culling throughout the entire dungeon.
Cache shared character geometry/materials with independent rigs.
Load the first encounter first and prefetch adjacent rooms and the boss before arrival.
Avoid loading every texture-quality variant at startup.
Use explicit cancellation, versioned requests, ownership/reference counts, failed-load fallbacks, and disposal.
Budget old and new assets simultaneously during quality changes.
Account for decoded images, geometry, textures, shadows, reflections, and postprocessing targets.
Keep Safari input, background suspension, recovery, and saved-quality behavior intact.
acceptance: No visible holes at doorways or through adjacent-room sight lines.
Repeated traversal and quality changes do not retain stale resources indefinitely.
Critical assets are ready before encounters without long main-thread stalls.
Measurements distinguish main-pass counts from complete-frame work and texture estimates from total GPU memory.

requirements.name: Visual, gameplay, and device validation
tasks: Run applicable TypeScript, source/generated JavaScript syntax, and production-build checks.
Run the existing gameplay/save/mobile suite and add focused rig, asset, compression, and lifecycle checks.
Validate complete 3D assets using structural and animation validation plus visual inspection.
Compare fixed before/after views and slow-motion attacks at equivalent settings.
Test cold/warm loads, unavailable assets/decoders, rapid quality switching, repeated encounters, death/respawn, background/resume, and renderer recovery.
Measure representative older and recent iPhones in portrait and landscape during at least 15 minutes of combat.
Record frame-time distributions, stalls, resource stability, and signs of thermal degradation.
Record unavailable browser or physical-device checks as pending; do not synthesize evidence.
acceptance: Automated checks pass or exact failures are reported with a concrete blocker.
Visual and numerical contact checks agree.
No regression in guest saves, economy, dungeon progression, controls, pause behavior, or recovery.
Device performance claims are supported by actual measurements.
Remaining incomplete assets and unverified quality gates are visible in the handoff.

requirements.name: Complete rollout and reviewable delivery
tasks: Apply the validated standard to all three archetypes and all five existing chambers.
Keep source assets, optimized runtime assets, provenance, budgets, and validation reports durably available.
Update character asset documentation and create an implementation report with evidence and known limitations.
Commit the exact verified source and follow supported Sites packaging/version workflows.
Keep the known-good combat release available for rollback.
Publish only under the executing request's authorization and confirm a terminal successful deployment before claiming the update is live.
acceptance: The result is a complete playable implementation, not just the prototype encounter.
All shipped references resolve and all claimed upgraded assets are actually installed.
The handoff distinguishes implemented, tested, pending, saved, and live states.
No unrelated source changes or audience changes are bundled into the release.

asset_contract.delivery_format: GLB/glTF 2.0 assets plus editable masters and source textures
asset_contract.budget_interpretation: Starting targets to validate, not mandatory minimum complexity or proof of frame-rate gains. Preserve quality with fewer triangles where possible.
asset_contract.lod_selection: Projected screen size with hysteresis; avoid conspicuous changes during close combat.

required_maps.name: orm
required_maps.content: Occlusion, roughness, and metallic channels verified against exporter/runtime conventions

optional_maps.name: emissive
optional_maps.usage: Localized eyes, embers, or armor fractures

source_reuse.higgsfield: Use existing designs and available suitable assets first. Generate missing references only through available, authorized tools. Do not assume 3D conversion, rigging, or PBR reconstruction capabilities.
source_reuse.external_assets: Use properly licensed models/materials and record the terms applicable to delivery in a browser game.
source_reuse.poly_haven: Retain suitable existing CC0 masonry and its provenance.
source_reuse.fallback: Keep procedural actors or a lower-resolution bundle for runtime failure, but do not count fallback-only actors as completed premium assets.

environment_contract.scope_cap_note: Do not manufacture filler to hit the cap; reuse assets where appropriate.
environment_contract.room_identity_rule: Apply these compositional ideas to the existing named rooms without renaming IDs, changing order, or adding chambers.
lighting_data: Static indirect lightmaps with dedicated UVs
Diffuse probe data for moving actors

quality_budgets.status: Proposed starting targets; tune using evidence.

units.triangles_and_draws: Main render pass unless explicitly stated
units.output: Actual render pixels, separate from CSS pixels

profiles.resolution_policy: Use a sustainable resolution and preserve explicit user selections.

caveats: Do not treat these values as universal Safari limits or measured results.
Material primitive budgets do not include all shadow/reflection/postprocessing passes.
Texture estimates are not total GPU memory; include render targets, buffers, decode peaks, and overlapping quality swaps.
Browser counters do not expose a universally exact GPU-byte total.
Texture compression and mesh transfer compression solve different problems.
Map proposed profiles onto the existing UI carefully; do not silently overwrite an explicit 4K preference.

texture_sizing_example.format: Uncompressed RGBA8 plus approximately a full mip chain

degradation_order: Reassess secondary texture detail while preserving hero silhouettes and attack readability

work_packages.name: Baseline
work_packages.exit_gate: Repeatable comparisons and known limitations are recorded.

work_packages.name: One-chamber look development
work_packages.exit_gate: Depth, material separation, and combat readability improve at equivalent resolution.

work_packages.name: Playable character slice
work_packages.exit_gate: Assets pass all-side and deformation inspection, and visible contact matches damage.

work_packages.name: Mobile production pipeline
work_packages.exit_gate: Reference encounter meets the selected measured budget or exact unresolved limits are documented.
work_packages.overlap: Introduce necessary compression and budget checks during P1/P2; do not postpone all optimization until the slice is oversized.

work_packages.name: Complete dungeon rollout
work_packages.exit_gate: All required content follows the reference quality standard, including the worst-case boss encounter.

work_packages.name: Release validation and handoff
work_packages.exit_gate: All required automated checks pass, visual/device evidence is available or explicitly pending, and release state is accurately reported.

source_checks.name: Production build
source_checks.instruction: Use the current applicable Sites build workflow; do not hardcode a stale plugin-cache path.

assets: Use Khronos glTF validation for structure, accessors, buffers, and animation; inspect unsupported-extension warnings.
Check finite bounds, scale, UV sets, texture channel/color-space assignment, sockets, skeleton independence, clips, and LOD references.
Validate actual loading of compressed and fallback bundles using pinned compatible decoders.
Verify all shipped asset paths and source/license records.
combat: Preserve strike order, stamina costs, buffer expiry, one queued input, phase timing, dodge commitment, and cancellation.
Test contact and integrated travel at 20, 30, 60, and 120 FPS sampling conditions.
Check capsule crossings/misses, parallel and degenerate segments, no windup damage, no duplicate target damage, behind-player exclusions, and wall clipping.
Check each attack against normal and boss-height actors at expected approach distances.
Inspect grip, shoulders, knees, feet, cape, and weapon position during full-speed and slow playback.
Verify that sharing geometry does not share animation state between actors.
visual: Capture entrance, character close-up, Warden combat, water, and boss views before/after under equivalent settings.
Inspect neutral and dungeon lighting, all sides of each actor, texture seams, material scale, highlights, and silhouettes.
Inspect camera movement and room transitions for aliasing, lighting pops, LOD pops, and missing geometry.
Inspect gates open/closed and shrines inactive/active for invalid baked lighting.
Keep attack telegraphs and touch controls readable at moderate phone brightness.
lifecycle: Asset/decoder load failures and playable fallback
Safari toolbar resizing and orientation changes
Save ownership, revision conflicts, equipment purchase validation, and reachable dungeon objectives

physical_devices.limitation_policy: If physical hardware or supported browser tooling is unavailable, record pending checks, deliver independently completed work, and never claim measured readiness.

conditional_followups.name: Foot placement / IK
conditional_followups.trigger: Basic rig, clips, and mobile budget are stable.
tasks: Prototype grounded feet and hand alignment where needed.
Keep the existing movement/collision contract and validate cost.

conditional_followups.name: Combat balance tuning
conditional_followups.trigger: Playtest evidence identifies a specific issue.
tasks: Propose targeted timing or stamina changes with before/after evidence.
Do not silently rebalance during asset integration.

conditional_followups.name: Explicit heavy-attack selection
conditional_followups.trigger: Separately requested mechanics expansion after core validation.
tasks: Define accessible desktop/touch input.
Validate recovery, resource costs, and combo interaction.

conditional_followups.name: Parry and block
tasks: Define timing, stamina, enemy responses, and accessible controls.
Run dedicated balance and mobile tests.

conditional_followups.name: Enemy feints
tasks: Define fair telegraphs and counterplay.
Avoid visually misleading existing guaranteed contact windows.

conditional_followups.name: Weapon-specific attack variants
tasks: Author reach, sockets, clips, and material responses per weapon.
Preserve one authoritative hit timeline and revalidate all contact cases.

not_default_upgrade_priorities: Full physical cloth simulation on every enemy
Default gameplay depth of field, heavy motion blur, film grain, chromatic aberration, or constant camera shake
Unrelated new quests, monetization, multiplayer, accounts, or dungeon layout changes

risk_register.risk: Inconsistent generated references or unusable generated meshes
risk_register.response: Use consistent art direction, validate complete geometry, and identify manual art work explicitly.

risk_register.risk: Concept lighting mistaken for albedo or surface height
risk_register.response: Author physical maps and inspect under neutral light.

risk_register.risk: Rig replacement breaks weapon contact or doubles movement
risk_register.response: Use a rig adapter, a shared phase clock, in-place clips, and collision-aware root movement.

risk_register.risk: Optimization removes sockets or flattens needed nodes
risk_register.response: Use selected transformations and validate names, hierarchy, animations, and sockets.

risk_register.risk: Baked shadows contradict gate or shrine state
risk_register.response: Separate static/dynamic contributions and test all state changes.

risk_register.risk: High-quality desktop assets exceed phone memory or thermal budget
risk_register.response: Compress textures, implement LOD/visibility, budget swap peaks, and perform sustained device tests.

risk_register.risk: Transparent atmosphere reduces frame rate and attack readability
risk_register.response: Limit coverage, pool effects, test worst-case combat, and scale by quality tier.

risk_register.risk: Asset streaming stalls combat or leaves missing content
risk_register.response: Prefetch required encounters, bound decoder concurrency, retain fallback, and record cold-load behavior.

risk_register.risk: A reference slice is delivered as the whole overhaul
risk_register.response: Track complete coverage of all three archetypes and five chambers before claiming completion.
